When a question refers to academic conferences, their names, homepages, or the papers presented at a specific conference.
When a question mentions scholarly journals, their titles, homepages, or articles published within a journal.
When a question seeks details about a paper such as title, abstract, year, citation count, reference count, or the venue (conference/journal) it appeared in.
When a question involves citation relationships, e.g., which works cite a given paper or how many citations a paper has received.
When a question is about research areas or topics and links authors, conferences, journals, publications, or keywords to a specific domain.
When a question asks about keywords associated with papers or domains, or searches for papers containing certain keywords.

activity_1.database_purpose: Tracks university activities and the participation of students and faculty in them.

rules.rule: When a question asks about activity names, IDs, or details of university events, clubs, or programs.
When a query concerns student personal information such as name, age, sex, major, advisor, or city code.
When a question seeks faculty details like name, rank, phone, office room, building, or sex.
When an inquiry is about which students or faculty are enrolled in a specific activity or the count of participants.
When a question links a student to their academic advisor or asks for the advisor of a given student.
When a query requests aggregated student demographics (age, sex, city code) within the context of activities.
When a question asks which faculty members participate in or supervise particular activities.

aircraft.database_purpose: Stores information about pilots, aircraft specifications, competition results, and airport traffic with aircraft‑airport relationships.

rules.rule: When a question asks about a pilot’s identity, age, or performance (e.g., “Who is the youngest pilot?” or “List pilots older than 40”), it targets the pilot entity.
When a query seeks details about aircraft models, descriptions, weight limits, or disk‑area specifications (e.g., “What is the max gross weight of the X‑15?”), it refers to the aircraft entity.
When the user mentions rounds, locations, dates, fastest qualifying times, or winning pilots/aircraft, the intent is about competition matches.
When the question involves passenger volumes, freight, aircraft movements, or changes over years for a specific airport, it concerns the airport entity.
When the request links aircraft to airports—such as “Which aircraft operate at JFK?” or “List airports that host the A320”—the intent is the airport‑aircraft relationship.

When a user compares specifications across aircraft (e.g., “Which aircraft has the highest max disk loading?”) or pilots (e.g., “Who has the most wins?”), the intent is a comparative performance analysis.
When the question asks about changes over time, such as passenger growth or freight trends at an airport, it signals a temporal trend analysis.

allergy_1.database_purpose: Tracks students, their majors, and any recorded allergies.

rules.rule: When a question asks for a list of allergy names, asks what allergies exist, or requests examples of allergies.
When a question seeks the classification or type of a specific allergy (e.g., food, medication, environmental).
When a question inquires which students have a particular allergy, or asks for students who share the same allergy.
When a question concerns personal or academic details of a student such as name, age, sex, major, city, or ID.
When a question requests counts or statistics about allergies across the student body (e.g., how many students are allergic to peanuts).
When a question involves linking a student to their academic advisor or asks for the advisor of a given student.

apartment_rentals.database_purpose: stores information about apartment buildings, individual units, their facilities, guests, and booking status.

rules.rule: when a query asks about building names, addresses, descriptions, managers or contact details, it refers to the Building entity.
when a question mentions unit numbers, types, bedroom/bathroom counts, or room totals, it signals intent toward the Apartment entity.
when a user inquires which amenities (e.g., gym, pool) a specific apartment has, the intent maps to the Apartment_Facilities entity.
when a request involves guest names, genders, ages or birth dates, it targets the Guests entity.
when a question concerns reservation dates, status codes, or which guest booked which apartment, it pertains to the Apartment_Bookings entity.
when a query asks whether a unit is available on a certain date or wants a list of currently vacant apartments, it refers to the View_Unit_Status view.

architecture.database_purpose: Provides information about architects and the bridges and mills they designed.

rules.rule: When the query asks for an architect's name, nationality, gender, or identifier, or seeks a list of architects, it signals the architect entity.
When the question mentions bridge name, location, length (in meters or feet), or asks for bridges designed by a specific architect, it signals the bridge entity.
When the query refers to mill name, type, location, built year, or notes, or requests mills created by a particular architect, it signals the mill entity.
When the user wants to retrieve all structures (bridges or mills) associated with a given architect, or to compare works across architects, the intent maps to the architectural works entity.
When the question focuses on the geographic location of bridges or mills, such as “which bridges are in Paris?” or “mills located in Yorkshire,” it signals a location‑based intent.
When the query involves bridge length measurements (meters or feet) or asks for size comparisons between bridges, it signals a dimensions‑related intent.
When the user asks for the built year of a mill or filters mills by year, it signals a construction‑year intent.

assets_maintenance.database_purpose: Tracks assets, their maintenance contracts, parts, faults, and engineering support.

rules.rule: When the query asks about third‑party companies, their types, addresses, or details of companies that supply or service assets.
When the question refers to maintenance contracts, start/end dates, or which contract is linked to a specific asset.
When the user mentions assets, asset make/model, acquisition or disposal dates, or which contract or supplier a particular asset belongs to.
When the request involves parts, part names, chargeability, amounts, or which parts are installed on an asset.
When the inquiry concerns fault logs, fault descriptions, timestamps, parts causing faults, or fault status updates.
When the question mentions maintenance engineers, their companies, skills, or visits to resolve faults.
When the query asks about skill codes, descriptions, or which skills are required to fix a particular part fault.

baseball_1.database_purpose: Baseball statistics and historical records for players, teams, awards, and venues.

rules.rule: When a question asks for a player's batting, pitching, or fielding numbers (e.g., hits, home runs, ERA, errors) for a season or career, it signals intent to query the batting, pitching, fielding, or related postseason tables.
When a query seeks a team's win‑loss record, ranking, runs scored, or other season totals, it points to the team, team_half, or team_franchise tables.
When the user mentions award winners, voting points, ties, or award years for players or managers, the intent maps to player_award, manager_award, player_award_vote, or manager_award_vote.
When the question asks whether a player is in the Hall of Fame, their induction year, voting totals, or category, it targets the hall_of_fame table.
When a request involves a player's contract amount, yearly salary, or salary comparisons, it signals the salary table.
When the user asks about playoff series results, round outcomes, or postseason team statistics, it refers to postseason, batting_postseason, pitching_postseason, or fielding_postseason.
When a query concerns a manager’s games managed, wins, losses, rank, or mid‑season changes, it points to the manager or manager_half tables.
When the question involves stadium names, locations, game attendance, or number of home games, it maps to the park and home_game tables.

battle_death.database_purpose: Records naval battles, participating ships, and associated deaths and injuries.

rules.rule: Questions about a specific engagement, its date, name, commanders, or overall result refer to the battle entity.
Inquiries about ship characteristics such as name, tonnage, type, location, or whether it was lost in a battle target the ship entity.
Requests for numbers of killed, injured, or notes on casualties linked to a ship point to the death entity.
Mentions of Bulgarian or Latin commanders, or queries about who led a battle, signal the commander aspect of the battle entity.
Questions about the result of a battle (victory, defeat, stalemate) map to the battle.result field.
When a query asks which ship caused a death or which deaths were caused by a particular ship, it refers to death.caused_by_ship_id linking to ship.

behavior_monitoring.database_purpose: Tracks student and teacher information, behavior incidents, and related detentions within a university setting.

rules.rule: When a question asks for a student's name, contact details, enrollment dates, or rental history, it signals intent to retrieve or filter data from the Students or Student_Addresses tables.
When a query mentions a teacher's identity, gender, contact information, or their involvement in notes or detentions, it points to the Teachers table (and related joins).
When the user refers to a behavior incident, its type, dates, summary, or recommendations, the intent targets the Behavior_Incident table (optionally joined with Ref_Incident_Type).

When a question involves detention assignments, types, start/end times, or links between students, teachers, and incidents, it maps to the Detention and Students_in_Detention tables (and Ref_Detention_Type).
When the request is about notes written by teachers for students, including dates or note text, it refers to the Assessment_Notes table.
When a query seeks address lines, city, zip, country, or address type details for students or teachers, it concerns the Addresses, Student_Addresses, and Ref_Address_Types tables.
When the user asks for descriptions of incident types, detention types, or address types, the intent is to read from the Ref_Incident_Type, Ref_Detention_Type, or Ref_Address_Types tables.

bike_1.database_purpose: Tracks bike‑share stations, real‑time bike/dock availability, trip histories, and associated weather conditions.

rules.rule: When the question asks about a station’s name, location (latitude/longitude), dock capacity, city, or installation date.
When the query concerns current bikes available, docks available, or timestamps of status updates for a given station.
When the user wants information on trip duration, start/end dates, start or end station names/IDs, bike IDs, subscription type, or rider zip code.
When the question references daily weather metrics such as temperature, humidity, pressure, wind speed, precipitation, cloud cover, or weather events, optionally linked to a zip code.
When the intent is to analyze trends over time, such as peak usage hours, most popular stations, average trip length, or correlation between weather and bike usage.
When the request involves spatial relationships, like finding stations within a city, nearest station to a coordinate, or trips that start/end in specific zip codes.
When the user asks about differences between subscriber and casual rider behavior, e.g., counts, average durations, or preferred stations.
When the question focuses on activity aggregated by zip code, such as total trips, average bikes available, or weather impact for that area.

body_builder.database_purpose: stores Olympic weight‑lifting results linked to personal demographic data for each athlete.

rules.rule: when a query asks for an athlete's Snatch, Clean Jerk, or Total lift values, it signals interest in the performance records.
when a question seeks an athlete's name, birth date, birth place, height, or weight, it refers to the personal demographic table.
when a request groups or filters athletes by their weight or height measurements, it targets the weight‑class or size attributes.
when a query ranks or compares athletes based on the summed Total column, it concerns overall competition results.
when a user asks for athletes born in a specific location or within a date range, the intent is to filter by Birth_Place or Birth_Date.
when a question involves calculating averages, maximums, or minima of Snatch, Clean Jerk, or Total across athletes, it pertains to statistical analysis of lift data.

book_2.database_purpose: Stores book titles, authors, issue counts, and their publication details such as publisher, date, and price.

rules.rule: When a question asks for a title, writer, or number of issues of a work, it refers to the book entity.
Mentions of author, writer, or creator map to the Writer column in the book table.
References to publishing house, publisher name, or who released the book correspond to the Publisher column in the publication table.
Queries about cost, price, or amount paid for a book relate to the Price column in the publication table.
When the user asks when a book was released, published, or the date of publication, it maps to Publication_Date.
Any request that combines book details with publisher, price, or date uses the Book_ID foreign key linking the book and publication tables.

browser_web.database_purpose: Tracks web client accelerators, browsers, and their compatibility details.

rules.rule: When the query asks about a web client accelerator's name, operating system, client type, or connection details.
When the question refers to browser names, market share percentages, or general browser information.
When the intent involves which browsers work with a specific accelerator or since which year they became compatible.
When the user wants to compare or list browsers based on their market share values.
When the query mentions the operating system supported by an accelerator.
When the question concerns the client type or connection characteristics of an accelerator.

candidate_poll.database_purpose: Stores poll results for political candidates together with basic demographic data of the people surveyed.

rules.rule: When a query asks about a candidate's poll numbers, support/consider/oppose/unsure percentages, or trends over time, it refers to this database.
When a question involves respondents' age, sex, height, weight, or other personal attributes linked to poll responses, it signals this database.
References to the polling organization (Poll_Source) or specific polling dates trigger usage of this schema.
Any request that identifies a candidate by name or People_ID and seeks related poll data maps to the candidate table.
When the intent is to compare or calculate average, max, min, or change in Support_rate across candidates or periods, this database is relevant.
Questions that contrast Consider_rate with Oppose_rate, or examine the distribution of Unsure_rate among respondents, belong to this dataset.

car_1.database_purpose: Stores car manufacturers, their models, vehicle performance specs, and related geographic information.

rules.rule: When a question asks about a car manufacturer’s name, full name, or country of origin, it signals the maker entity.
When a query references a specific car model, asks for models produced by a maker, or seeks the relationship between makes and models, it targets the model entity.
When the user requests MPG, horsepower, weight, cylinders, acceleration, or year for a vehicle, the intent relates to the vehicle specifications entity.
When the question involves continents, countries, or the location of a maker or model, it points to the geographic entity.
When the user wants a list of all models for a given maker or wants to enumerate makers that produce a particular model, the model_list entity is relevant.
When the query seeks to match a make identifier with its corresponding make and model names, or to translate between make IDs and names, it concerns the car_name_lookup entity.

chinook_1.database_purpose: stores information for a digital music store, covering tracks, albums, artists, customers, employees, and sales invoices.

rules.rule: questions about album titles, which artist released an album, or listing albums in the catalog
queries seeking artist names, the artists behind specific albums or tracks, or a list of all performers

cinema.database_purpose: Store details about films, cinemas, and their daily show schedules.

rules.rule: When the query asks for a film's title, director, original air date, production code, or its position in a series/season.
When the question seeks a cinema's name, opening year, seating capacity, or location.

When the request involves the price of a film screening at a particular cinema and date.
When the intent mentions a film's rank within a series or its episode number in a season.
When the user asks about how many seats a cinema can accommodate or compares capacities between cinemas.

city_record.database_purpose: Provides city demographics, economic data, climate statistics, and sports match information for Chinese cities.

rules.rule: When the query asks for a city's name, population, GDP, or its Chinese characters (Hanzi/Pinyin), it refers to the city table.
When the question seeks monthly temperature values or average climate data for a specific city, it targets the temperature table.
When the user mentions a match date, venue, score, result, or competition, the intent is about the match table.
When the request involves which city hosted a particular match or the year a city hosted an event, it concerns the hosting_city table.
Any request for regional population or GDP figures for a city maps to the city table's economic columns.
When the question combines city attributes (e.g., population) with match or hosting information, the intent requires joining city, match, and hosting_city tables.

climbing.database_purpose: Stores information about mountains and climbers, including mountain characteristics and climbing performance records.

rules.rule: Any query about a mountain’s name, height, prominence, range, or country refers to the mountain entity.
Questions that mention a climber’s name, nationality, total points, or personal climbing time target the climber entity.
When a question links a climber to a specific mountain (e.g., who climbed X or which mountain did Y climb), it signals a climbing record intent.
Requests for the tallest mountains, highest prominence, or ordering mountains by height or prominence invoke ranking intents on the mountain table.
Queries asking for top climbers by points, fastest ascent times, or leaderboards for a country trigger performance‑ranking intents.
Any question that restricts results by country or mountain range (e.g., mountains in the Alps, climbers from Japan) uses geographic filtering.
Requests for averages, totals, or counts such as average mountain height, total points per country, or number of climbs per range invoke aggregate calculations.

club_1.database_purpose: Tracks students, clubs, and their membership details within a university.

rules.rule: When the question asks about a student's personal data (name, age, sex, major, city, or advisor), it refers to the Student entity.
When the query seeks information about a club's name, description, or location, it targets the Club entity.
When the request involves which students belong to which clubs, positions held, or membership counts, it concerns the Member_of_club relationship.
When the question mentions a faculty advisor linked to a student, it signals the Advisor attribute within the Student table.
When the user filters or groups students by their field of study, the intent relates to the Major column of the Student table.
When the inquiry references where a club meets or a student's city code, it points to ClubLocation in Club or city_code in Student.

coffee_shop.database_purpose: Tracks coffee shop locations, staff, performance, members, and happy‑hour promotions.

rules.rule: When the question asks about a coffee shop’s address, opening year, staff count, or overall rating, it refers to the shop entity.
When the query involves customer names, ages, membership cards, membership levels, or purchase timestamps, it signals the member entity.
When the user asks about monthly happy‑hour periods, which shop hosts them, or how many staff oversee the event, it maps to the happy_hour table.
When the question concerns which members joined a specific happy‑hour, or how much each member spent during that promotion, it targets the happy_hour_member linking table.
Any request that combines a shop with the number of staff assigned to a happy‑hour (e.g., “how many staff were in charge during July happy hour”) points to the Num_of_shaff_in_charge column.
When the intent is to calculate total or average spending of members during happy‑hour events, it uses the Total_amount field linked to members.

college_1.database_purpose: Tracks college courses, class sections, departments, faculty, students, and enrollment records.

rules.rule: When the query asks about a course code, description, credit value, or department affiliation, it refers to the COURSE table.
When the question mentions class times, rooms, sections, or which professor teaches a specific class, it signals intent toward the CLASS table.
References to department names, codes, school affiliation, or department contact details map to the DEPARTMENT table.
Queries about faculty members, their employee numbers, offices, extensions, or highest degree use the PROFESSOR (and EMPLOYEE) tables.
When the user asks about a student's personal data, GPA, credit hours, class standing, or assigned advisor, it targets the STUDENT table.
Questions about which students are enrolled in a class, their grades, or class rosters correspond to the ENROLL table.

When the question is about student IDs, names, majors (department), total earned credits, or grades received.
When the intent is to find or set the advising relationship between a student and an instructor.
When a query asks for day-of-week, start/end times, or the definition of a time slot identifier.

college_3.database_purpose: Stores information about college students, faculty, departments, courses, enrollments, minors, and grade conversion.

rules.rule: When a question seeks a student's name, age, sex, major, advisor, or city code, it refers to the Student entity.
When a query asks for a faculty member's name, rank, contact details, office location, or building, it targets the Faculty entity.
When the request involves department numbers, divisions, names, rooms, buildings, or phone numbers, it concerns the Department entity.
When the user mentions course identifiers, titles, credit values, instructors, schedule days/hours, or department affiliation, it maps to the Course entity.
When the question asks which students are enrolled in which courses, or what grades they received, it pertains to the Enrolled_in relationship.
When the query involves students pursuing a minor in a specific department, it refers to the Minor_in relationship.
When the user wants to translate letter grades to numeric grade points, it uses the Gradeconversion table.

company_1.database_purpose: manage employee, department, and project information for a company

concert_singer.database_purpose: Stores information about stadium venues, singers, concerts, and which singers performed at each concert.

rules.rule: When a question asks about stadium locations, capacities, or statistical aggregates (highest, lowest, average) of attendance, it signals the venue entity.
When a query concerns a singer’s personal details (name, country, age, gender) or their songs (title, release year), it targets the artist entity.
When the user refers to a concert’s name, theme, year, or asks for concerts held at a specific stadium, the intent maps to the event entity.
When the question links singers to concerts—e.g., which singers performed at a concert, or which concerts featured a particular singer—it invokes the lineup relationship.
When the request asks for comparative or aggregate data about stadium capacities (e.g., largest stadium, average capacity across locations), it signals attendance statistics.
When the user seeks lists of songs by a singer, filters by release year, or compares song counts across singers, the intent relates to the song catalog within the artist entity.

county_public_safety.database_purpose: Provides county‑level public safety statistics and city demographic breakdowns for a county.

rules.rule: When the question asks for general information about a county such as its name, population, total police force, or location.
When the query mentions police officers, staffing ratios, residents per officer, or case burden for a county.
When the user refers to crime rate, crime statistics, or any safety performance indicator tied to a county.
When the request involves racial or ethnic composition (White, Black, Asian, etc.) of cities within the county.
When the question seeks the population or name of a city that belongs to a specific county.
When the intent connects a county to its cities, such as listing all cities in a county or aggregating city data for a county.

course_teach.database_purpose: stores courses, teachers, and the assignments of teachers to courses with grade levels and start dates.

rules.rule: when a question seeks the course name, ID, or basic description of a class, it signals interest in the course entity
when a query asks for a teacher's name, age, hometown, or teacher ID, it points to the teacher entity

cre_Doc_Control_Systems.database_purpose: Tracks the lifecycle, drafting, and distribution of controlled documents within an organization.

rules.rule: When a query mentions kinds of documents, classifications, or codes (e.g., "what are the document types?"), it refers to the Ref_Document_Types table.

When the user refers to the party that ships or forwards documents, asks for agent names or codes, or mentions shipping details, the intent maps to Ref_Shipping_Agents and its foreign key in Documents.

When the conversation involves draft numbers, versions, copies, or the process of creating and circulating drafts (e.g., "show draft 3 of document 12"), it targets Document_Drafts, Draft_Copies, and Circulation_History.
When a query mentions staff members, their roles, or who handled a document (e.g., "which manager reviewed draft 2?"), it points to Employees and Roles, possibly joined through Circulation_History.

When the user asks about where or when a document was mailed, recipient addresses, or mailing dates (e.g., "when was document 5 mailed and to which address?"), it refers to Documents_Mailed and Addresses.

cre_Doc_Tracking_DB.database_purpose: Tracks documents, their types, storage locations, responsible employees, and destruction schedules.

When the inquiry is about project identifiers and their descriptive details (e.g., "What is the Project_ID and its details?" or "Show information for project 5.")

cre_Drama_Workshop_Groups.database_purpose: Manage drama workshop groups, their bookings, related customers, performers, products, services, and financial documents.

cre_Theme_park.database_purpose: Stores details about theme‑park attractions, hotels, locations, visitors and related entities.

customer_deliveries.database_purpose: Tracks customers, their orders, product catalog, and delivery logistics.

customers_campaigns_ecommerce.database_purpose: Tracks customers, their addresses, orders, products, and marketing mailshot campaigns for an e‑commerce platform.

debate.database_purpose: Stores information about political debates, their venues, audiences, and the participating candidates.

decoration_competition.database_purpose: Stores information about colleges, their members, and round results in a decoration competition.

rules.rule: When a question asks for details about a college—its name, leader, or location—or wants a list of colleges, it maps to the college table.
When a query concerns participants (members), their personal info such as name, country, or which college they belong to, it targets the member table.
When the user refers to a competition round, its identifier, the decoration theme used, or the ranking of a member within that round, the round table is relevant.
Any request about the decoration themes—e.g., which themes were used, theme popularity, or theme per round—signals the Decoration_Theme column in the round table.

When a query links members to their colleges (e.g., “which college does a member represent?”), it requires joining member.College_ID with college.College_ID.
Inquiries about who leads a college or searching for colleges led by a specific person map to the Leader_Name column of the college table.

department_management.database_purpose: Tracks departments, their budgets, rankings, and the heads who manage them.

rules.rule: When a question asks about department names, creation dates, rankings, budgets, or employee counts, it signals interest in the department entity.

When the question involves which head is assigned to which department, or whether a head is acting temporarily, it targets the management relationship.
Any request for total, average, or comparative budget figures (in billions) across departments points to financial aspects of the department entity.
When users ask for top‑ranked departments, rank ordering, or rank‑based filters, the intent relates to department rankings.
Questions about changing, listing, or verifying the current head of a department, especially involving temporary acting status, map to the management table.
Inquiries about the number of employees in a department, or comparisons of employee counts between departments, refer to the Num_Employees column of the department entity.

department_store.database_purpose: Tracks department‑store chain operations, including stores, staff, customers, products, suppliers, and orders.

When a question references order IDs, status codes, dates, or the items contained in an order, it maps to the order entity.

When a request involves department names within a store, the department's ID, or which staff are assigned to a department, it indicates the department entity.

device.database_purpose: Tracks mobile devices, their software details, retail shops, and inventory levels.

rules.rule: When the question asks about a device's model, carrier, software platform, applications, or package version.

document_management.database_purpose: Manage documents, their hierarchical structures, associated functional areas, sections, and related images with user access control.

dog_kennels.database_purpose: Tracks dogs in a kennel, their owners, breeds, sizes, treatments, professionals, and related charges.

dorm_1.database_purpose: Manage student housing assignments, dorm details, and amenities.

driving_school.database_purpose: Manage driving school operations including students, instructors, lessons, vehicles, payments, and addresses.

election.database_purpose: Stores county demographics, political party officeholders, and election details for a jurisdiction.

film_rank.database_purpose: Tracks films, their studios/directors, and box‑office estimates across international markets.

When the user asks for a flight number, source airport, destination airport, or the airline operating a specific route, the intent maps to the flight_route entity.

Queries that seek airports within a particular city or country, or that request the airport code for a city, correspond to the airport_location intent.

Requests to translate an airline's full name to its abbreviation or vice‑versa map to the abbreviation_lookup intent.

flight_4.database_purpose: Provides information about airline routes, airports, and airlines for flight planning and analysis.

When the question mentions airport names, cities, countries, IATA/ICAO codes, or geographic coordinates, it targets the airports table.
When the user seeks details such as airline name, IATA/ICAO code, callsign, country of origin, or active status, the intent maps to the airlines table.
Any request about whether a route is operated jointly by multiple airlines or includes a codeshare flag points to the codeshare column in routes.

formula_1.database_purpose: Provides detailed historical data about Formula 1 circuits, races, drivers, constructors, and race results.

game_injury.database_purpose: Tracks stadium details, game results, and player injuries linked to specific matches.

student_transcripts_tracking.database_purpose: Tracks students, their enrolments, courses, and official transcripts within an academic institution.

rules.rule: When a query asks about a person's name, ID, contact details, registration dates, or status (active/inactive), it refers to the Students table.
When a question mentions current or permanent residence, city, zip, or country for a student, it signals the Addresses table linked via current_address_id or permanent_address_id.
When the intent involves course titles, descriptions, or looking up which courses belong to a section or program, it maps to the Courses table (and possibly Sections).
When a user asks about a program of study, its department, or the summary name/description, the focus is on Degree_Programs and its link to Departments.
When the question concerns which semester a student is enrolled in, what program they are pursuing, or the list of courses they are taking, it targets Student_Enrolment and Student_Enrolment_Courses.
When the request is about official transcript dates, contents, or which courses appear on a transcript, it points to Transcripts and Transcript_Contents.

swimming.database_purpose: Stores information about swimmers, venues, competitions, and performance records.

rules.rule: When a query asks about an athlete’s name, nationality, or personal times for any of the listed distances (100‑700 m), it refers to the swimmer entity.
When a question mentions a venue’s name, capacity, city, country, or opening year, it signals interest in the stadium entity.
When the user refers to a competition name, the year it took place, or the stadium where it was held, the intent targets the event entity.
When the request seeks the result of a specific swimmer in a particular event, or asks for the best recorded time for an event, it concerns the record entity.
When a question compares times across the 100 m, 200 m, …, 700 m columns or asks for the fastest distance for a swimmer, it maps to the distance performance attributes within the swimmer table.
When the user wants to list all events a swimmer participated in, or retrieve all records set at a given stadium or year, the intent involves joining event, swimmer, and record data.

theme_gallery.database_purpose: Tracks artists, their exhibitions, and attendance statistics for a themed gallery.

rules.rule: When the question asks about an artist’s name, country, age, or the year they joined the gallery.
When the query mentions exhibition year, theme, ticket price, or wants to list exhibitions.
When the user seeks daily attendance numbers, total visitors, or trends for a specific exhibition.
When the request connects an artist to the exhibitions they participated in or asks which artists are in a given exhibition.
When the question involves comparing ticket prices across exhibitions or calculating revenue from ticket sales.
When the user asks about changes over time, such as how attendance or exhibition themes have evolved year‑by‑year.

tracking_grants_for_research.database_purpose: Tracks research grants, associated organisations, projects, staff, documents and outcomes.

rules.rule: When a query mentions funding amounts, grant start/end dates, or which organisation received a grant.
When the question refers to institutions, their types, details, or which grants/projects belong to them.
When the user asks about project identifiers, linked organisations, project details, or associated tasks.
When the request involves sent dates, response dates, document types, or documents tied to a specific grant.
When the inquiry concerns staff members, their roles, project assignments, employment organisations, or date ranges of involvement.
When the question mentions research or project outcomes, outcome codes, descriptions, or outcome details linked to a project.
When the user asks about tasks within a project, task identifiers, or specific task details such as objectives.

tracking_orders.database_purpose: Tracks customers, their orders, related invoices, products, and shipment details.

rules.rule: Queries that ask for customer names, IDs, contact or profile information, or link customers to their orders.
Questions about order IDs, status, placement dates, or which customer placed a specific order.
Requests for invoice numbers, dates, details, or the relationship between invoices and orders/shipments.
Inquiries about product IDs, names, descriptions, or which products appear in particular orders.
Mentions of shipment tracking numbers, dates, shipment IDs, or how shipments relate to orders and invoices.
Questions concerning items within an order, their status, product association, or detailed line‑item information.
Queries that link specific order items to shipments, such as which items are in a given shipment.

tracking_share_transactions.database_purpose: Tracks investors, their share lots, and buy/sell transactions.

rules.rule: When the query mentions investors, investor details, or asks who holds which shares or lots.
When the question refers to share lots, lot identifiers, or asks which lots belong to an investor or transaction.
When the user asks about buying, selling, amounts, dates, share counts, or any activity recorded in the Transactions table.
When the intent involves transaction categories, codes, or descriptions such as "purchase", "sale", or other types defined in Ref_Transaction_Types.
When the query specifically mentions sales details, sales transactions, or wants information from the Sales table.
When the question focuses on purchase details, purchase transactions, or requests data from the Purchases table.
When the user wants to know how transactions map to lots, i.e., which lot(s) are associated with a given transaction or vice‑versa.

tracking_software_problems.database_purpose: Tracks software problems, their categories, status, related products, staff assignments, and log entries.

rules.rule: When a question asks about a software issue itself—its description, report or closure dates, or which product it affects—it signals the problem entity.
When a query mentions problem categories, category codes, or category descriptions, it refers to the category entity.
When a question involves the current or historical state of a problem—status codes or status descriptions—it points to the status entity.
When a user asks about product names, details, or which problems are linked to a specific product, the product entity is relevant.
When a question concerns staff members—who reported, is assigned to, or authorized closure of a problem—it signals the staff entity.
When a query seeks log entries, entry dates, descriptions, fixes, or other log details for a problem, it pertains to the log entity.

train_station.database_purpose: Provides information about train stations, their passenger statistics, and which trains serve them.

rules.rule: When a question asks for a station's name, location, number of platforms, or main services offered, it signals interest in basic station details.
When a query mentions annual entry/exit counts, interchanges, or total passenger numbers, it targets the station's passenger statistics.
When a user asks about a train's name, departure/arrival time, or the service type it belongs to, the intent relates to train scheduling information.
When a question seeks to know which trains stop at a particular station or which stations a specific train serves, it refers to the train‑station relationship.
When the inquiry focuses on the type of service (e.g., regional, intercity) provided by a train or available at a station, it concerns service details.
When a request combines passenger volumes with platform counts to assess capacity or planning needs, it signals a capacity‑planning intent.

tvshow.database_purpose: Provides information about TV channels, series episodes, and cartoons, including broadcast details, ratings, and production credits.

rules.rule: When a query asks about a TV channel’s name, country, language, content type, picture format (e.g., pixel aspect ratio, HD), pay‑per‑view options, or package offerings, it maps to the TV_Channel table.
When a question references an episode number, air date, rating, share, 18‑49 demographic share, viewer count, weekly rank, or the channel that aired it, the intent targets the TV_series table.
When a user asks for a cartoon’s title, director, writer, original air date, production code, or the channel that broadcast it, the intent relates to the Cartoon table.
Any request for viewership statistics such as total viewers (in millions), rating/share numbers, or weekly ranking for a series episode should be interpreted as seeking data from TV_series.
Questions about technical broadcast specifications—pixel aspect ratio, high‑definition status, or pay‑per‑view availability—signal intent toward the TV_Channel table.

When the user inquires about when a series episode or cartoon first aired, or the schedule of episodes on a specific channel, the intent maps to the Air_Date fields in TV_series or Original_air_date in Cartoon.
Queries that mention production codes, series IDs, or cartoon IDs indicate a need to retrieve identifiers from the respective tables (TV_series.id, Cartoon.id, TV_Channel.id).

twitter_1.database_purpose: stores Twitter‑style user profiles, follow relationships, and tweet records.

rules.rule: when a question asks who follows whom, mutual follows, or follower/followee counts, it signals the follow relationships stored in the follows table.
when a query involves tweet text, hashtags, keywords, or the content of messages posted by users, it refers to the tweets table.
when a request asks for tweets by date, recent posts, or chronological ordering of a user's messages, it targets the createdate column in the tweets table.
when a question seeks a user's name, email, partition identifier, or other profile attributes, it points to the user_profiles table.
when a query asks for the number of followers a user has, ranking by follower count, or comparing follower totals, it uses the followers column in user_profiles (and may join with follows).

university_basketball.database_purpose: stores university basketball team season statistics together with basic university information.

rules.rule: when a question asks about a team's win‑loss record, winning percentages, or home/road performance for ACC games or all games.
when a question seeks a university's location, founding year, enrollment size, nickname, affiliation, or primary conference.
when a question compares ACC regular‑season results to overall season results, or asks how a team performed inside vs. outside the ACC.
when a question mentions a team name, asks which school a team belongs to, or references a School_ID/Team_ID.
when a question inquires about games played at neutral venues or the neutral‑site win percentage for a team.
when a question requests overall statistics across all teams, such as total games, average percentages, or league‑wide home/road trends.

voter_1.database_purpose: Stores phone‑based votes for a contest, linking voters' area codes to states and contestants.

rules.rule: When the question asks which state corresponds to a given area code or wants to list area codes for a state.
When the query seeks details about contestants, such as their numbers, names, or a list of all contestants.
When the user wants to retrieve, count, or filter individual votes by vote ID, phone number, state, contestant, or date.
When the question involves aggregating votes per state, such as total votes per state or ranking states by vote count.
When the intent is to summarize votes per contestant, like total votes received, votes by state, or trends over time.

voter_2.database_purpose: Stores student demographic details and their voting choices across election cycles.

rules.rule: When a query asks about a student's name, age, sex, major, advisor, or city code, it targets the Student table.
When a question references votes for President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, Class President, or Class Senator, it concerns the Voting_record table.
Any request that mentions an election year, term, or cycle and wants to filter or aggregate votes by that period should be mapped to the Election_Cycle column in Voting_record.
Queries about when a student registered to vote, registration timelines, or date ranges relate to the Registration_Date field.
When a user wants to see which student cast which vote, or to combine demographic data with voting choices, the intent is to join Student.StuID with Voting_record.StuID.
Questions that ask for students under a particular advisor or to list votes grouped by advisor pertain to the Advisor column in the Student table.

wedding.database_purpose: Tracks marriages, the people involved, and the churches where ceremonies occurred.

rules.rule: Any query about an individual's name, age, gender, or country that mentions marriage or spouse signals interest in the people table.
Questions asking who married whom, the male and female participants of a wedding, or details about a specific pair refer to the wedding table.
When a question mentions the year of a wedding, the church where it took place, or the date of the ceremony, it targets the wedding table (and possibly the church table for venue info).
Inquiries about a church's name, its organizer, opening date, or whether it continues another church relate to the church table.
Requests for weddings that happened in a particular year or range of years map to the Year column in the wedding table.
If a query asks about the countries of the bride or groom, or compares nationalities across marriages, it involves the Country column in the people table linked through the wedding table.

wine_1.database_purpose: stores data on U.S. wines, their grape varieties, appellations, and market metrics.

rules.rule: when a question asks about grape types, colors, or characteristics of the grapes used in wines
when a query references wine regions, counties, states, AVA status, or geographic area of production
when the user seeks details about a specific wine such as name, winery, vintage year, or drinking window
when the question involves the cost of a wine, price ranges, or price comparisons
when the intent is to retrieve or compare wine ratings, scores, or critic evaluations
when the user asks about the number of cases produced, available inventory, or sales volume

workshop_paper.database_purpose: Stores information about workshops, paper submissions, and their acceptance outcomes.

rules.rule: When the query asks about workshop names, dates, venues, or lists of workshops, it signals interest in the workshop entity.
When the question references paper scores, authors, colleges, or submission identifiers, it pertains to the submission entity.
When the user wants to know whether a submission was accepted or rejected for a specific workshop, or wants to see all results linking submissions to workshops, the acceptance entity is relevant.
Any request for the author of a particular submission or for submissions by a given author maps to the author information within the submission table.
Questions that ask for counts, averages, or other aggregates of submissions grouped by college refer to the college column in the submission table.
When the user asks when a workshop occurs or wants the venue for a specific workshop date, the query targets the Date and Venue columns of the workshop table.

world_1.database_purpose: Provides geographic, demographic, and political information about countries, cities, and languages worldwide.

rules.rule: When the query asks about a city’s name, district, population, or its country code, it refers to the city table.

When the question involves a nation’s name, continent, region, surface area, independence year, population, life expectancy, GNP, government form, head of state, or capital city, it targets the country table.
When the user asks which languages are spoken in a country, their official status, or the percentage of speakers, the intent maps to the countrylanguage table.
If the query seeks the name of a country’s capital or asks which country a given city serves as capital, it links the capital column in the country table to the city table.
Any request for comparative population, density, life expectancy, or GNP figures across cities or countries triggers demographic analysis using population fields from city and country tables.
When the question groups or filters nations by continent, region, or government form, it pertains to the country table’s Continent, Region, or GovernmentForm columns.
Queries about a country’s year of independence or historical changes in GNP refer to the IndepYear or GNPOld columns in the country table.

wrestler.database_purpose: Stores information about wrestlers, their championship reigns, event participation, and elimination details.

rules.rule: When a question seeks a wrestler's personal or reign information—such as name, number of reigns, days held, home location, or associated event—the intent maps to the wrestler table.
When a query asks how a wrestler was eliminated, who eliminated them, the move used, or the exact time of elimination, it targets the elimination table.
When a user inquires about the team a wrestler belonged to during an elimination, or asks for teammates of a specific wrestler, the relevant concept is the Team column in the elimination table.

When the question involves comparative or aggregate data about reigns—e.g., longest reign, total days held across wrestlers, or ranking by days held—it pertains to the Reign and Days_held columns of the wrestler table.

When a request asks which wrestlers participated in a particular event, what events a wrestler has been part of, or overall event outcomes, the intent relates to the Event column in the wrestler table.
When a user wants a list of all eliminations involving a specific wrestler, including dates/times and opponents, the query should draw from the elimination table linked by Wrestler_ID.

wta_1.database_purpose: Stores professional women's tennis player bios, match results, and historical rankings.

rules.rule: When a query asks for a player's name, birth date, handedness, country code, or other personal attributes, it refers to the players table.
When a question seeks the winner or loser of a specific match, the score, round, surface, or tournament details, it targets the matches table.
When the intent mentions tournament name, ID, level, draw size, or date (including year), the query is about tournament metadata stored in matches.
When a user wants a player's ranking on a given date, ranking points, or ranking changes over time, the request maps to the rankings table.
When the question compares winner/loser ages, hand, height, entry type, seed, or rank within a match, it combines player attributes with match outcomes.
When the query asks for match duration (minutes), best‑of format, or number of matches played in a round, it pertains to numeric fields in the matches table.

yelp.database_purpose: Provides business listings, reviews, categories, check‑ins, tips and neighbourhood information for Yelp‑style services.

rules.rule: When the question asks for a restaurant, shop, or other venue's name, address, city, state, rating, open status, or geographic coordinates.
When the query seeks the types or cuisines a business belongs to, such as “Italian”, “coffee shop”, or any other category label.
When the user wants textual reviews, star ratings, or temporal trends (year/month) written by customers for a specific business.
When the question references a reviewer’s identity, name, or activity across multiple businesses (e.g., “reviews by user X”).
When the intent involves how often or on which days a business receives check‑ins, including total counts per day of week.
When the request mentions a local area, district, or neighbourhood name to locate businesses within that region.
When the query asks for short user‑generated tips, their like counts, or the time (year/month) they were posted for a business.
